description: Build a queue-based multi-step processing mode for /Users/imyu/.claude/orchestrator/scripts/onboard-learn.js, modeled on the judge cursor pattern. Problem: the current --max-candidates cap is architecturally wrong — on large repos (cosma-ai-studio: 2457 candidates), the cap destroys coverage (150 kept only 20 notes, kb_earned 13%). Fix: (1) New subcommand/flag: onboard-learn.js --enqueue --out <dir> reads all mined notes from --in <dir> and writes a queue file (<dir>/onboard-queue.json: {pending:[...all candidates...], kept:[], rejected:[], cursor:0, total:N}). (2) onboard-learn.js --drain --batch 50 --out <dir>: reads queue, processes the next --batch candidates through the existing LLM keep/reject logic, updates kept/rejected/cursor in place, exits. Re-runnable: safe to call repeatedly until cursor==total. (3) onboard-learn.js --inject --confirm can already work from onboard-notes.json; after drain completes write final onboard-notes.json from queue.kept as before. (4) Add --queue-status flag: prints {total, processed:cursor, kept:len(kept), remaining:total-cursor, done:cursor==total}. (5) Remove --max-candidates or keep it as a hard emergency cap only (default: none). Follow orch-gate: write to /tmp, cp into place.
